title: A genome-wide screen identifies genes required for erythroid differentiation
model: HUDEP-2 cells, GeCKOv2 genome-scale and focused secondary CRISPR-KO libraries
contrast: Orthochromatic (D12) vs proerythroblast (D0), genome-scale screen, paired by replicate (3 vs 3); secondary library run separately
paper_calls: 277 genes required for terminal erythroid differentiation; NHLRC2 and VAC14 named, VAC14 validated in vivo
barcs_calls: Genome-scale: 0 genes at FDR 0.10 after control calibration (0 against the centred control null). Secondary: 729 at FDR 0.10 (485 depleted; 940 against the control null).
named_hits: Genome-scale: NHLRC2 #78 depleted (effect -1.30, raw p 0.055, FDR 1), VAC14 not depleted; ALAS2/UROD depleted in effect but FDR 1. Secondary: VAC14 #67 depleted (FDR 2.6e-10), GATA1 #273, ALAS2 #3; NHLRC2 not in library.
verdict: In the genome-scale screen 46.6% of non-targeting guides reach p<0.05, so calibrating to the controls collapses the whole list to 0 genes at FDR 0.10 (even ALAS2/UROD) and neither named gene passes, though NHLRC2 is depleted in effect (not a contradiction). The validated gene VAC14 is recovered cleanly in the focused secondary library at FDR 2.6e-10.
